o1.biggest_strength: It gives Monsoon Dark buyers their own track, with a draft that names the blend and the roasters' closest match, and it holds ex-subscribers behind a 93% on-time gate, so it treats the real reasons people left rather than reaching for discounts.
o1.biggest_mistake: It leads with the 91 to 180 day group and handles the 9,000 slipping 46 to 90 day buyers only as a side day-28 nudge, leaving the cheapest group to win back out of the waves and out of the value sum.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the 46 to 90 day group wave one with a no-discount reminder, size its value, and back the 70% reachable figure with real email and WhatsApp overlap data.

o2.biggest_strength: Its order follows the data: slipping 46 to 90 day buyers first with no code, Monsoon Dark next, and ex-subscribers gated on delivery and date choice. Its contacted counts, ₹385 at the 15% cap and 13%-weighted ₹535 for subscribers all check out.
o2.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark first email asks for a quiz instead of naming the closest match, and the 365+ day group gets 15% off in a single email with no test of whether that discount pays.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the recommended match in the Monsoon Dark email, put the quiz second, and test the 365+ day offer at 0% against 15% before rolling it out.

reason: Both find the discontinued blend and the courier problem, but the second starts with the cheap-to-win slipping buyers, keeps its maths conservative and checkable, and adds a pre-order idea for Monsoon Dark that I wouldn't have come up with.
